summary: The City Council unanimously approved the "Thrive Local Initiative," a small business support program offering grants, mentorship, and workshops to local businesses. Applications open October 15, 2023, with eligibility limited to businesses with fewer than 50 employees and a valid city business license. The city will track outcomes, publish an annual report, and plans future projects including an incubator, ecommerce platform, and co-working space.
one_line: The City Council launched the Thrive Local Initiative, offering grants, mentorship, and workshops to small businesses, after a unanimous September 27, 2023 vote.
key_facts: The City Council voted unanimously on September 27, 2023 to establish the "Thrive Local Initiative."
The proposal was spearheaded by Councilor Maria Gonzales and seconded by Councilor Calvin Roberts.
The Thrive Local Initiative begins offering resources on October 13, 2023, including grants, mentorship, and tailored workshops.
Applications open October 15, 2023 and are reviewed on a rolling basis.
Eligibility requires fewer than 50 employees, a valid city business license, and a plan for growth or substantiation within the local community.
The city has set up a dedicated help desk, operational from the launch date, to assist applicants with questions.
Workshops will cover marketing, financial literacy, supply chain management, and digital transformation.
Rachel Freeman, who runs an independent bookstore, said grants could help modernize her business with new technology and marketing strategies.
Joshua Kim, owner of a small tech startup, highlighted the value of mentorship from experienced entrepreneurs.
A study by the city's Economic Development Office found about 67 cents of every dollar spent at a small business stays in the local community, versus 40 cents for larger retail chains.
The City Council and the Department of Economic Development will track businesses assisted, jobs created, return on investment, and overall economic growth.
The city commits to a publicly available annual report on the program's impact and success stories.
Future plans include a business incubator, an ecommerce platform for local products, and a co-working space for freelancers and remote workers.
Residents can give feedback through town hall meetings, surveys, and direct contact with council members and city officials.
